notes: Summary: Enterprise insurer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) to replace proof-of-concept on prem setup.
Primary ask: full Private VPC deployment with SSO (SAML) + SCIM user provisioning and RBAC in console/control plane.
Data constraints: regulated PII, must remain in us-east-1; legal requests contractual data residency + retention controls.
Security: require KMS integration (customer-managed keys), audit log streaming to SIEM (Splunk), SOC2 evidence for product and infra.
Performance targets: 99th pct latency < 150ms for embed/rerank flows, sustained throughput ~300 qps during business hours, burst to 1k qps.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit reserved capacity if net savings >25% vs current infra TCO.
Model preference: prefer open Llama-variant quantized to int8 for document embeddings + a smaller LLM for agent tasks; fallback policy to hosted smaller model if dedicated pool saturated.
Control plane requirements: need per-team RBAC, SCIM group sync, SAML IdP integration (Okta + Azure AD), audit trails for admin actions.
Recent: security questionnaire submitted 2026-02-28 (see drive doc), security team requested KMS architecture diagram + key lifecycle SOPs.
Quote from CISO: 'We can't accept vendor keys; need HSM-backed CMKs and a clear key rotation plan.'
POC plan: 4-week private VPC POC — week1 network+peering, week2 SSO/SCIM + RBAC, week3 KMS + audit pipelines, week4 load tests and regression evals.
Notes from sales call 2026-02-25: SE committed to produce architecture diagram and example Terraform for VPC peering; pushed to deliver by 2026-03-08.
Action items: collect sample SAML metadata from Helix IdP, request AAD/Okta SCIM schema, schedule SIEM integration call with platform team.
Risks: legal may require additional contract language delaying close by 4-6 weeks; network department slow to provide peering CIDR ranges.
Internal: prioritize Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching + KV cache to hit throughput targets with fewer GPUs.
How they differentiate: moving from heavy on-prem ops — want Redwood to be 'production-ready' runtime with clear runbook and auditability.

Operational: runbook + DR plan, playbooks for failover to hosted lower-tier model
